units.proposition: Each supervisory authority shall, when deciding whether to impose an administrative fine and on the amount in each individual case, give due regard to the categories of personal data affected by the infringement.

units.ru_label: Due regard: manner infringement became known; notification extent
units.action: give due regard to the manner in which the infringement became known to the supervisory authority
units.scope: including whether, and to what extent, the controller or processor notified the infringement
units.temporal: when deciding whether to impose an administrative fine and when deciding on the amount in each individual case
units.proposition: Each supervisory authority shall, when deciding whether to impose an administrative fine and on the amount in each individual case, give due regard to the manner in which the infringement became known to the supervisory authority, including whether, and to what extent, the controller or processor notified the infringement.

units.ru_label: Due regard: compliance with prior Article 58(2) measures on same subject-matter
units.action: give due regard to compliance with previously ordered measures under Article 58(2) against the controller or processor with regard to the same subject-matter
units.scope: administrative fines decisions under Article 83
units.temporal: when deciding whether to impose an administrative fine and when deciding on the amount in each individual case
units.proposition: Each supervisory authority shall, when deciding whether to impose an administrative fine and on the amount in each individual case, give due regard to whether the controller or processor complied with measures previously ordered under Article 58(2) with regard to the same subject-matter.

units.ru_label: Due regard: adherence to codes of conduct or certification mechanisms
units.action: give due regard to adherence to approved codes of conduct or approved certification mechanisms
units.scope: codes of conduct approved pursuant to Article 40 and approved certification mechanisms under the GDPR
units.temporal: when deciding whether to impose an administrative fine and when deciding on the amount in each individual case
units.proposition: Each supervisory authority shall, when deciding whether to impose an administrative fine and on the amount in each individual case, give due regard to adherence to approved codes of conduct or approved certification mechanisms.

units.action: determine specific conditions for the processing of national identification numbers or other identifiers of general application
units.scope: processing of national identification numbers or other identifiers of general application
units.proposition: Member States have the power to further determine specific conditions for processing national identification numbers or other identifiers of general application.

units.action: use national identification numbers or other identifiers of general application only under appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of the data subject
units.scope: use/processing of national identification numbers or other identifiers of general application pursuant to the GDPR
units.condition: where a Member State has determined specific conditions for processing such identifiers
units.proposition: Where a Member State has determined specific conditions for processing such identifiers, controllers shall use national identification numbers or other identifiers of general application only under appropriate safeguards for the data subject’s rights and freedoms pursuant to the GDPR.

units.ru_label: Disclosure of personal data in official documents
units.addressee: public authorities, public bodies, and private bodies performing a task carried out in the public interest that hold official documents
units.action: disclose personal data contained in official documents they hold
units.scope: personal data in official documents held for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest
units.condition: the disclosure is made in accordance with Union or Member State law to which the public authority or body is subject and aims to reconcile public access to official documents with the right to the protection of personal data pursuant to the GDPR
units.proposition: A public authority, public body, or private body performing a task in the public interest that holds official documents may disclose personal data contained in those documents in accordance with applicable Union or Member State law, to reconcile public access to official documents with the right to the protection of personal data.

units.ru_label: MS may adopt secrecy-specific SA power rules
units.action: adopt specific rules to set out the powers of the supervisory authorities laid down in points (e) and (f) of Article 58(1) in relation to certain controllers or processors
units.scope: controllers or processors that are subject to an obligation of professional secrecy or equivalent obligations of secrecy under Union or Member State law or rules established by national competent bodies
units.condition: where necessary and proportionate to reconcile the right to the protection of personal data with the obligation of secrecy
units.proposition: Member States may adopt specific rules setting out the supervisory authorities’ powers under Article 58(1)(e) and (f) in relation to controllers or processors subject to professional or equivalent secrecy obligations, where this is necessary and proportionate to reconcile data protection with secrecy.

units.ru_label: Limit application of adopted rules to secrecy‑obtained data
units.action: apply rules adopted under Article 90(1) to personal data other than data received or obtained in an activity covered by the secrecy obligation
units.scope: rules adopted pursuant to Article 90(1)
units.proposition: Member States shall not apply the rules adopted under Article 90(1) to personal data other than personal data that a controller or processor received or obtained in an activity covered by the secrecy obligation.

units.ru_label: Notify adopted rules to Commission by 25 May 2018
units.action: notify to the Commission the rules adopted pursuant to Article 90(1)
units.condition: upon adoption of rules pursuant to Article 90(1)
units.temporal: by 25 May 2018
units.proposition: Each Member State shall notify to the Commission the rules adopted pursuant to Article 90(1) by 25 May 2018.

units.action: notify to the Commission any subsequent amendment affecting the rules adopted pursuant to Article 90(1)
units.condition: when an amendment affecting the rules adopted pursuant to Article 90(1) occurs
units.temporal: without delay
units.proposition: Each Member State shall notify to the Commission without delay any subsequent amendment affecting the rules adopted pursuant to Article 90(1).

units.action: reconcile by law the right to the protection of personal data under this Regulation with the right to freedom of expression and information
units.scope: including processing for journalistic purposes and for academic, artistic or literary expression
units.proposition: Member States must, by law, reconcile the right to the protection of personal data under this Regulation with the right to freedom of expression and information, including for processing for journalistic, academic, artistic or literary purposes.

units.action: provide for exemptions or derogations from Chapters II, III, IV, V, VI, VII and IX of the GDPR
units.scope: processing carried out for journalistic purposes or for academic, artistic or literary expression
units.condition: if necessary to reconcile the right to the protection of personal data with the freedom of expression and information
units.proposition: For processing carried out for journalistic or for academic, artistic or literary expression, Member States must provide for exemptions or derogations from Chapters II, III, IV, V, VI, VII and IX where necessary to reconcile data protection with freedom of expression and information.

units.action: notify the Commission of the provisions of its law adopted pursuant to paragraph 2
units.proposition: Each Member State must notify the Commission of the provisions of its law adopted pursuant to Article 85(2).

units.action: notify the Commission of any subsequent law or amendment affecting the provisions adopted pursuant to paragraph 2
units.temporal: without delay
units.proposition: Each Member State must, without delay, notify the Commission of any subsequent law or amendment affecting the provisions adopted pursuant to Article 85(2).

units.action: provide more specific rules by law or by collective agreements
units.scope: to ensure the protection of rights and freedoms in respect of the processing of employees' personal data in the employment context, particularly for recruitment; performance of the contract of employment (including discharge of legal or collectively agreed obligations); management, planning and organisation of work; equality and diversity in the workplace; health and safety at work; protection of employer's or customer's property; exercise and enjoyment of employment-related rights and benefits; and termination of the employment relationship
units.proposition: Member States may, by law or by collective agreements, provide for more specific rules to ensure the protection of rights and freedoms in respect of the processing of employees' personal data in the employment context for the listed employment-related purposes.

units.addressee: Member States and social partners concluding collective agreements under Article 88(1)
units.action: include suitable and specific measures to safeguard data subjects' human dignity, legitimate interests and fundamental rights in those rules
units.scope: with particular regard to transparency of processing, transfers of personal data within a group of undertakings or a group of enterprises engaged in a joint economic activity, and monitoring systems at the workplace
units.condition: when adopting rules under Article 88(1)
units.proposition: When adopting rules under Article 88(1), Member States and social partners concluding collective agreements shall include suitable and specific measures to safeguard the data subject's human dignity, legitimate interests and fundamental rights, with particular regard to transparency of processing, intra‑group transfers of personal data, and monitoring systems at the workplace.

units.action: notify to the Commission the provisions of its law adopted pursuant to Article 88(1)
units.temporal: by 25 May 2018
units.proposition: Each Member State shall notify to the Commission, by 25 May 2018, the provisions of its law adopted pursuant to Article 88(1).

units.action: notify to the Commission any subsequent amendment affecting the provisions adopted pursuant to Article 88(1)
units.scope: amendments affecting national provisions adopted pursuant to Article 88(1)
units.temporal: without delay
units.proposition: Each Member State shall notify to the Commission, without delay, any subsequent amendment affecting the provisions of its law adopted pursuant to Article 88(1).

units.action: subject processing to appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of the data subject
units.scope: appropriate safeguards in accordance with the GDPR
units.condition: when processing personal data for archiving in the public interest, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes
units.proposition: Controllers must, when processing personal data for archiving in the public interest, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes, subject the processing to appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of the data subject in accordance with the GDPR.

units.action: ensure technical and organisational measures are in place to respect the principle of data minimisation
units.scope: safeguards for processing under Article 89(1)
units.condition: when applying safeguards for processing for archiving in the public interest, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes
units.proposition: Controllers must, when applying safeguards for processing for archiving in the public interest, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes, ensure technical and organisational measures are in place to respect the principle of data minimisation.

units.action: include pseudonymisation among the technical and organisational measures
units.scope: measures implemented under the safeguards to ensure data minimisation
units.condition: provided that the archiving in the public interest, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes can be fulfilled in that manner
units.proposition: Controllers may include pseudonymisation among the technical and organisational measures, provided that the archiving in the public interest, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes can be fulfilled in that manner.

units.action: fulfil the purposes by further processing that does not permit, or no longer permits, the identification of data subjects
units.scope: processing for archiving in the public interest, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes
units.condition: where those purposes can be fulfilled by such further processing
units.proposition: Controllers must, where archiving in the public interest, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes can be fulfilled by further processing that does not permit or no longer permits identification of data subjects, fulfil those purposes in that manner.

units.action: provide for derogations from data subject rights in Articles 15, 16, 18 and 21
units.scope: processing for scientific or historical research purposes or statistical purposes
units.condition: subject to the conditions and safeguards in Article 89(1), and only insofar as those rights are likely to render impossible or seriously impair the achievement of the specific purposes and such derogations are necessary for the fulfilment of those purposes
units.proposition: Union or Member State legislators may, for processing for scientific or historical research purposes or statistical purposes, provide for derogations from data subject rights in Articles 15, 16, 18 and 21 subject to the conditions and safeguards in Article 89(1) and only insofar as the rights would render impossible or seriously impair achieving the specific purposes and the derogations are necessary to fulfil those purposes.

units.action: provide for derogations from data subject rights in Articles 15, 16, 18, 19, 20 and 21
units.scope: processing for archiving purposes in the public interest
units.condition: subject to the conditions and safeguards in Article 89(1), and only insofar as those rights are likely to render impossible or seriously impair the achievement of the specific purposes and such derogations are necessary for the fulfilment of those purposes
units.proposition: Union or Member State legislators may, for processing for archiving purposes in the public interest, provide for derogations from data subject rights in Articles 15, 16, 18, 19, 20 and 21 subject to the conditions and safeguards in Article 89(1) and only insofar as the rights would render impossible or seriously impair achieving the specific purposes and the derogations are necessary to fulfil those purposes.

units.addressee: controllers relying on derogations under Article 89(2) or (3)
units.action: apply those derogations to processing for another purpose
units.scope: derogations provided under Article 89(2) and (3)
units.condition: where processing referred to in Article 89(2) or (3) serves at the same time another purpose
units.proposition: Controllers relying on derogations under Article 89(2) or (3) are prohibited, where the processing at the same time serves another purpose, from applying those derogations to processing for that other purpose.

units.ru_label: Construe references to repealed Directive as this Regulation
units.action: construe references to Directive 95/46/EC as references to this Regulation
units.condition: when interpreting or applying texts that contain references to the repealed Directive 95/46/EC
units.proposition: References to Directive 95/46/EC must be construed as references to this Regulation.

units.ru_label: Construe references to Article 29 Working Party as EDPB
units.action: construe references to the Working Party on the Protection of Individuals with regard to the Processing of Personal Data established by Article 29 of Directive 95/46/EC as references to the European Data Protection Board established by this Regulation
units.condition: when interpreting or applying texts that contain references to the Article 29 Working Party
units.proposition: References to the Article 29 Working Party must be construed as references to the European Data Protection Board.

units.ru_label: No additional GDPR obligations where ePrivacy applies
units.action: impose additional obligations on natural or legal persons
units.scope: in relation to processing in connection with the provision of publicly available electronic communications services in public communication networks in the Union
units.condition: for matters for which those persons are subject to specific obligations with the same objective under Directive 2002/58/EC
units.proposition: This Regulation is prohibited from imposing additional obligations on natural or legal persons regarding processing connected to the provision of publicly available electronic communications services in public communication networks in the Union where those persons are already subject to specific obligations with the same objective under Directive 2002/58/EC.

units.action: be assisted by a committee
units.proposition: The European Commission is obliged to be assisted by a committee.

units.action: ensure that the assisting committee is a committee within the meaning of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011
units.condition: for the committee referred to in paragraph 1
units.proposition: The European Commission is obliged to ensure that the assisting committee is a committee within the meaning of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011.

units.action: apply Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011
units.condition: where reference is made to paragraph 2 of this Article
units.proposition: When reference is made to paragraph 2 of this Article, Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011 must be applied.

units.action: apply Article 8 of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011
units.condition: where reference is made to paragraph 3 of this Article
units.proposition: When reference is made to paragraph 3 of this Article, Article 8 of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011 must be applied.

units.ru_label: Previously concluded data-transfer agreements remain in force
units.action: recognise the continued validity of specified international agreements
units.scope: international agreements involving the transfer of personal data to third countries or international organisations
units.condition: the agreement was concluded by a Member State prior to 24 May 2016 and complied with Union law applicable prior to that date
units.temporal: until the agreement is amended, replaced or revoked
units.proposition: Member States shall recognise the continued validity of international agreements involving transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations that were concluded before 24 May 2016 and complied with Union law applicable at that time, until those agreements are amended, replaced or revoked.

units.ru_label: Existing church rules may continue if aligned
units.addressee: churches and religious associations or communities
units.action: continue to apply their pre-existing comprehensive data-protection rules
units.scope: in a Member State
units.condition: the entities applied such comprehensive rules at the time of entry into force of this Regulation and the rules are brought into line with this Regulation
units.proposition: Churches and religious associations or communities may continue to apply their pre-existing comprehensive data-protection rules in a Member State if those rules were in force at the time of entry into force of this Regulation and are brought into line with this Regulation.

units.addressee: churches and religious associations or communities
units.action: bring their pre-existing comprehensive data-protection rules into line with this Regulation
units.scope: in a Member State
units.condition: if they wish to continue to apply such comprehensive rules that were in force at the time of entry into force of this Regulation
units.proposition: Churches and religious associations or communities must bring their pre-existing comprehensive data-protection rules into line with this Regulation in a Member State if they wish to continue to apply rules that were in force at the time of entry into force of this Regulation.

units.action: be subject to the supervision of an independent supervisory authority
units.condition: they apply comprehensive rules in accordance with Article 91(1)
units.proposition: Churches and religious associations must be subject to the supervision of an independent supervisory authority when they apply comprehensive rules in accordance with Article 91(1).

units.action: designate a specific independent supervisory authority for supervising churches and religious associations that apply comprehensive rules under Article 91(1)
units.condition: the designated specific authority fulfils the conditions laid down in Chapter VI of this Regulation
units.proposition: Member States may designate a specific independent supervisory authority to supervise churches and religious associations that apply comprehensive rules under Article 91(1), provided that the authority fulfils the conditions laid down in Chapter VI of this Regulation.

units.action: adopt delegated acts
units.condition: subject to the conditions laid down in Article 92
units.proposition: The European Commission has the power to adopt delegated acts subject to the conditions laid down in Article 92.

units.action: exercise the delegated power referred to in Article 12(8) and Article 43(8)
units.scope: for an indeterminate period of time
units.temporal: from 24 May 2016
units.proposition: The European Commission has the delegated power referred to in Article 12(8) and Article 43(8) for an indeterminate period starting on 24 May 2016.

units.action: revoke the delegation of power referred to in Article 12(8) and Article 43(8)
units.exception: Revocation shall not affect the validity of any delegated acts already in force.
units.temporal: at any time
units.consequence: A revocation decision ends the delegation of power specified in the decision and takes effect the day after its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union or on a later date specified in the decision.
units.proposition: The European Parliament has the power to revoke at any time the delegation of power referred to in Article 12(8) and Article 43(8), with the revocation decision ending the specified delegation and taking effect the day after its publication or on a later specified date, without affecting the validity of any delegated acts already in force.

units.action: revoke the delegation of power referred to in Article 12(8) and Article 43(8)
units.exception: Revocation shall not affect the validity of any delegated acts already in force.
units.temporal: at any time
units.consequence: A revocation decision ends the delegation of power specified in the decision and takes effect the day after its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union or on a later date specified in the decision.
units.proposition: The Council of the European Union has the power to revoke at any time the delegation of power referred to in Article 12(8) and Article 43(8), with the revocation decision ending the specified delegation and taking effect the day after its publication or on a later specified date, without affecting the validity of any delegated acts already in force.

units.action: notify the delegated act it adopts to the European Parliament and the Council simultaneously
units.scope: simultaneous notification to the European Parliament and the Council
units.condition: upon adopting a delegated act
units.temporal: as soon as it adopts the delegated act
units.proposition: As soon as it adopts a delegated act, the European Commission is obligated to notify that act simultaneously to the European Parliament and the Council.

units.action: express an objection to a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 12(8) and Article 43(8)
units.condition: after notification of the delegated act to the European Parliament and the Council
units.temporal: within three months of notification
units.consequence: An objection expressed within that period prevents the delegated act from entering into force.
units.proposition: The European Parliament has the power to express an objection to a delegated act within three months of its notification, and an objection expressed within that period prevents the delegated act from entering into force.

units.action: express an objection to a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 12(8) and Article 43(8)
units.condition: after notification of the delegated act to the European Parliament and the Council
units.temporal: within three months of notification
units.consequence: An objection expressed within that period prevents the delegated act from entering into force.
units.proposition: The Council of the European Union has the power to express an objection to a delegated act within three months of its notification, and an objection expressed within that period prevents the delegated act from entering into force.

units.action: inform the Commission that it will not object to a delegated act
units.condition: after notification of the delegated act
units.temporal: before the expiry of the three-month objection period
units.consequence: Together with the Council doing the same before expiry, this enables the delegated act to enter into force.
units.proposition: The European Parliament has the power to inform the Commission before the expiry of the three-month period that it will not object to a delegated act, which together with the Council doing the same enables the delegated act to enter into force.

units.action: inform the Commission that it will not object to a delegated act
units.condition: after notification of the delegated act
units.temporal: before the expiry of the three-month objection period
units.consequence: Together with the European Parliament doing the same before expiry, this enables the delegated act to enter into force.
units.proposition: The Council of the European Union has the power to inform the Commission before the expiry of the three-month period that it will not object to a delegated act, which together with the European Parliament doing the same enables the delegated act to enter into force.

units.action: initiate the extension by three months of the objection period for a delegated act
units.temporal: before the expiry of the initial three-month objection period
units.consequence: The objection period is extended by three months.
units.proposition: The European Parliament has the power, before the expiry of the initial three-month objection period, to initiate an extension of that period by three months, which extends the objection period by three months.

units.action: initiate the extension by three months of the objection period for a delegated act
units.temporal: before the expiry of the initial three-month objection period
units.consequence: The objection period is extended by three months.
units.proposition: The Council of the European Union has the power, before the expiry of the initial three-month objection period, to initiate an extension of that period by three months, which extends the objection period by three months.

units.addressee: delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 12(8) and Article 43(8)
units.action: enter into force
units.condition: unless neither the European Parliament nor the Council has expressed an objection within three months of notification, or both the European Parliament and the Council have informed the Commission before the expiry of that period that they will not object
units.proposition: A delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 12(8) and Article 43(8) is prohibited from entering into force unless neither the European Parliament nor the Council has objected within three months of notification or both have informed the Commission before expiry that they will not object.

units.ru_label: Commission to propose amendments to other data-protection acts
units.action: submit legislative proposals with a view to amending other Union legal acts on the protection of personal data
units.scope: to ensure uniform and consistent protection of natural persons with regard to processing; in particular concerning rules on processing by Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies, and on the free movement of such data
units.condition: if appropriate
units.proposition: The Commission is obligated, if appropriate, to submit legislative proposals to amend other Union legal acts on the protection of personal data in order to ensure uniform and consistent protection of natural persons with regard to processing, in particular concerning rules on processing by Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies and on the free movement of such data.

units.action: submit a report on the evaluation and review of this Regulation
units.scope: to the European Parliament and the Council
units.temporal: by 25 May 2020 and every four years thereafter
units.proposition: By 25 May 2020 and every four years thereafter, the European Commission shall submit to the European Parliament and the Council a report on the evaluation and review of this Regulation.

units.action: make the reports public
units.scope: reports on the evaluation and review of this Regulation
units.proposition: The European Commission shall make the reports on the evaluation and review of this Regulation public.

units.action: examine the application and functioning of Chapter V on the transfer of personal data to third countries or international organisations
units.scope: with particular regard to decisions adopted pursuant to Article 45(3) GDPR and decisions adopted on the basis of Article 25(6) of Directive 95/46/EC
units.condition: in the context of the evaluations and reviews referred to in paragraph 1
units.proposition: In the context of the evaluations and reviews referred to in paragraph 1, the European Commission shall examine the application and functioning of Chapter V on the transfer of personal data to third countries or international organisations, with particular regard to decisions adopted pursuant to Article 45(3) GDPR and decisions adopted on the basis of Article 25(6) of Directive 95/46/EC.

units.action: examine the application and functioning of Chapter VII on cooperation and consistency
units.condition: in the context of the evaluations and reviews referred to in paragraph 1
units.proposition: In the context of the evaluations and reviews referred to in paragraph 1, the European Commission shall examine the application and functioning of Chapter VII on cooperation and consistency.

units.action: request information from Member States and supervisory authorities
units.condition: for the purpose of paragraph 1
units.proposition: For the purpose of paragraph 1, the European Commission may request information from Member States and supervisory authorities.

units.action: take into account the positions and findings of the European Parliament, the Council, and other relevant bodies or sources
units.condition: in carrying out the evaluations and reviews referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2
units.proposition: When carrying out the evaluations and reviews referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2, the European Commission shall take into account the positions and findings of the European Parliament, the Council, and other relevant bodies or sources.

units.action: submit appropriate proposals to amend this Regulation
units.scope: in particular taking into account developments in information technology and the state of progress in the information society
units.condition: if necessary
units.proposition: If necessary, the European Commission shall submit appropriate proposals to amend this Regulation, in particular taking into account developments in information technology and the state of progress in the information society.

units.action: treat the Regulation as binding in its entirety
units.scope: in all Member States
units.temporal: from 25 May 2018
units.proposition: Member States must treat the Regulation as binding in its entirety.

units.action: apply the Regulation directly without requiring national transposition measures
units.scope: in all Member States
units.temporal: from 25 May 2018
units.proposition: Member States must apply the Regulation directly without requiring national transposition measures.

units.ru_label: No referral at request of time-barred person
units.action: refer a question on the validity of a Board decision to the Court of Justice at the request of a natural or legal person
units.scope: validity of a decision of the European Data Protection Board
units.condition: the requesting natural or legal person had the opportunity to bring an action for annulment of that decision, in particular because it was directly and individually concerned, but did not bring such an action
units.temporal: within the period laid down in Article 263 TFEU
units.proposition: A national court is prohibited from referring a question on the validity of an EDPB decision to the Court of Justice at the request of a natural or legal person that could have brought an annulment action, in particular if directly and individually concerned, but did not do so within the time limit laid down in Article 263 TFEU.

units.addressee: court seized of proceedings against a decision by a supervisory authority
units.action: contact the competent court in another Member State to confirm the existence of related proceedings
units.scope: proceedings against a decision by a supervisory authority
units.condition: the seized court has reason to believe that proceedings concerning the same processing are brought before a competent court in another Member State
units.proposition: A court seized of proceedings against a decision by a supervisory authority is obliged to contact the competent court in another Member State to confirm the existence of related proceedings when it has reason to believe that proceedings concerning the same processing are brought there.

units.addressee: any court other than the court first seized
units.action: stay its proceedings
units.condition: related proceedings are pending before a court in another Member State
units.proposition: Any court other than the court first seized is permitted to stay its proceedings when related proceedings are pending before a court in another Member State.

units.addressee: any court other than the court first seized
units.action: decline jurisdiction in favour of the court first seized
units.condition: related proceedings are pending before a court in another Member State and, on request of one of the parties, the court first seized has jurisdiction and its law permits consolidation of the related proceedings
units.proposition: Any court other than the court first seized is permitted to decline jurisdiction in favour of the court first seized when related proceedings are pending in another Member State, upon request of a party, provided the first court has jurisdiction and its law permits consolidation.

units.action: treat proceedings as related
units.condition: the proceedings are so closely connected that it is expedient to hear and determine them together to avoid the risk of irreconcilable judgments from separate proceedings
units.proposition: Courts are obliged to treat proceedings as related where they are so closely connected that it is expedient to hear and determine them together to avoid the risk of irreconcilable judgments from separate proceedings.

units.action: bring the action before the courts of the Member State where the controller or processor has an establishment or where the data subject resides
units.scope: proceedings against a controller or processor
units.exception: unless the controller is a public authority of a Member State acting in the exercise of its public powers
units.proposition: In proceedings against a controller or processor, the plaintiff has the right to bring the action before the courts of the Member State where the controller or processor has an establishment or where the data subject resides, unless the controller is a public authority acting in the exercise of its public powers.

units.action: compensate any damage suffered by a person as a result of processing that infringes this Regulation
units.condition: a person suffers damage as a result of processing that infringes this Regulation
units.proposition: A controller or processor is obliged to compensate any damage suffered by a person as a result of processing that infringes this Regulation.

units.action: be exempt from liability for damage caused by processing
units.condition: the controller or processor proves that it is not in any way responsible for the damage
units.proposition: A controller or processor has the right to be exempt from liability for damage caused by processing if it proves that it is not in any way responsible for the damage.

units.action: interpret the concept of damage broadly in light of the case-law of the Court of Justice to reflect the objectives of this Regulation
units.scope: assessment of compensation claims under this Regulation
units.proposition: Courts are obliged to interpret the concept of damage broadly in light of the case-law of the Court of Justice in a manner that fully reflects the objectives of this Regulation.

units.action: treat processing that infringes delegated or implementing acts adopted under this Regulation or Member State laws specifying rules of this Regulation as processing that infringes this Regulation
units.scope: determination of infringement and liability
units.proposition: Courts are obliged to treat processing that infringes delegated or implementing acts adopted under this Regulation or Member State laws specifying rules of this Regulation as processing that infringes this Regulation.

units.action: receive full and effective compensation for the damage suffered
units.condition: the data subject has suffered damage as a result of processing that infringes this Regulation
units.proposition: A data subject has the right to receive full and effective compensation for the damage suffered as a result of processing that infringes this Regulation.

units.action: hold each controller or processor liable for the entire damage
units.condition: controllers or processors are involved in the same processing
units.proposition: Courts are obliged to hold each controller or processor liable for the entire damage where controllers or processors are involved in the same processing.

units.action: apportion compensation according to the responsibility of each controller or processor for the damage caused by the processing
units.condition: the controllers or processors are joined to the same judicial proceedings in accordance with Member State law and full and effective compensation of the data subject is ensured
units.proposition: Courts are permitted to apportion compensation according to the responsibility of each controller or processor for the damage caused by the processing when they are joined to the same judicial proceedings in accordance with Member State law and full and effective compensation of the data subject is ensured.

units.action: institute recourse proceedings against other controllers or processors involved in the same processing
units.condition: the controller or processor has paid full compensation
units.temporal: subsequently
units.proposition: A controller or processor that has paid full compensation has the right to subsequently institute recourse proceedings against other controllers or processors involved in the same processing.

units.action: allow general jurisdiction rules to prejudice the application of specific jurisdiction rules contained in this Regulation
units.scope: proceedings seeking a judicial remedy, including compensation, against a controller or processor
units.condition: this Regulation contains specific rules on jurisdiction applicable to the proceedings
units.proposition: Courts are prohibited from allowing general jurisdiction rules to prejudice the application of specific jurisdiction rules contained in this Regulation where those rules apply to proceedings seeking a judicial remedy, including compensation, against a controller or processor.

units.action: impose penalties, including administrative fines, for infringements of this Regulation, in addition to or instead of appropriate measures under this Regulation
units.scope: enforcement of this Regulation
units.condition: an infringement of this Regulation has occurred
units.proposition: A supervisory authority is obliged to impose penalties, including administrative fines, for infringements of this Regulation, in addition to or instead of appropriate measures under this Regulation.

units.action: issue a reprimand instead of a fine
units.scope: enforcement action selection
units.condition: the case concerns a minor infringement or the likely fine would constitute a disproportionate burden to a natural person
units.proposition: A supervisory authority is permitted to issue a reprimand instead of a fine where the case concerns a minor infringement or the likely fine would constitute a disproportionate burden to a natural person.

units.action: give due regard to the nature, gravity and duration of the infringement, the intentional character, actions taken to mitigate damage, degree of responsibility, any relevant previous infringements, how the infringement became known, compliance with measures ordered, adherence to a code of conduct, and any other aggravating or mitigating factor
units.scope: setting and imposing penalties including administrative fines
units.proposition: A supervisory authority is obliged to give due regard to specified aggravating and mitigating factors when setting and imposing penalties including administrative fines.

units.action: subject the imposition of penalties, including administrative fines, to appropriate procedural safeguards in accordance with the general principles of Union law and the Charter, including effective judicial protection and due process
units.scope: penalty proceedings under this Regulation
units.proposition: Authorities imposing penalties are obliged to subject the imposition of penalties, including administrative fines, to appropriate procedural safeguards in accordance with the general principles of Union law and the Charter, including effective judicial protection and due process.

units.action: lay down rules on criminal penalties for infringements of this Regulation, including for infringements of national rules adopted pursuant to and within the limits of this Regulation
units.scope: national legislation
units.proposition: Member States have the power to lay down rules on criminal penalties for infringements of this Regulation, including for infringements of national rules adopted pursuant to and within the limits of this Regulation.

units.action: provide that criminal penalties allow deprivation of profits obtained through infringements of this Regulation
units.scope: national criminal penalty design
units.proposition: Member States have the power to provide that criminal penalties allow deprivation of profits obtained through infringements of this Regulation.

units.action: impose criminal penalties for infringements of national rules adopted pursuant to this Regulation and administrative penalties in a manner that leads to a breach of the principle of ne bis in idem
units.scope: enforcement of this Regulation and national implementing rules
units.proposition: Member States are prohibited from imposing criminal penalties for infringements of national rules adopted pursuant to this Regulation and administrative penalties in a manner that leads to a breach of the principle of ne bis in idem, as interpreted by the Court of Justice.

units.action: impose administrative fines
units.scope: administrative penalties for infringements of this Regulation
units.proposition: Each supervisory authority has the power to impose administrative fines for infringements of this Regulation.

units.action: determine the amount of administrative fines in each individual case, taking into account all relevant circumstances, with due regard in particular to the nature, gravity and duration of the infringement and its consequences, and the measures taken to ensure compliance and to prevent or mitigate the consequences of the infringement
units.scope: setting administrative fines
units.proposition: A supervisory authority is obliged to determine the amount of administrative fines in each individual case, taking into account all relevant circumstances, with due regard in particular to the nature, gravity and duration of the infringement and its consequences, and the measures taken to ensure compliance and to prevent or mitigate the consequences of the infringement.

units.action: understand an undertaking, for the purpose of imposing administrative fines on an undertaking, in accordance with Articles 101 and 102 TFEU
units.scope: cases where administrative fines are imposed on an undertaking
units.proposition: A supervisory authority is obliged to understand an undertaking, for the purpose of imposing administrative fines on an undertaking, in accordance with Articles 101 and 102 TFEU.

units.action: take account of the general level of income in the Member State and the economic situation of the person when considering the appropriate amount of a fine on a person that is not an undertaking
units.scope: cases where administrative fines are imposed on persons that are not an undertaking
units.proposition: A supervisory authority is obliged to take account of the general level of income in the Member State and the economic situation of the person when considering the appropriate amount of a fine on a person that is not an undertaking.

units.action: use the consistency mechanism to promote a consistent application of administrative fines
units.scope: coordination under this Regulation
units.proposition: A supervisory authority is permitted to use the consistency mechanism to promote a consistent application of administrative fines.

units.action: determine whether and to what extent public authorities are subject to administrative fines
units.scope: national rules on the applicability of administrative fines to public authorities
units.proposition: Member States have the power to determine whether and to what extent public authorities are subject to administrative fines.

units.action: apply rules on administrative fines so that in Denmark fines are imposed by competent national courts as criminal penalties and in Estonia fines are imposed by the supervisory authority in a misdemeanour procedure
units.scope: national enforcement arrangements
units.condition: the application has an equivalent effect to administrative fines imposed by supervisory authorities
units.proposition: Denmark and Estonia have the power to apply rules on administrative fines so that in Denmark fines are imposed by competent national courts as criminal penalties and in Estonia fines are imposed by the supervisory authority in a misdemeanour procedure, provided this has an equivalent effect to administrative fines imposed by supervisory authorities.

units.action: take into account the recommendation by the supervisory authority initiating the fine
units.scope: Denmark
units.proposition: Competent national courts in Denmark are obliged to take into account the recommendation by the supervisory authority initiating the fine.

units.action: ensure that fines imposed are effective, proportionate and dissuasive
units.scope: imposition of fines under or in connection with this Regulation
units.proposition: Authorities imposing fines are obliged to ensure that the fines imposed are effective, proportionate and dissuasive.

units.action: implement a system that provides for effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties
units.scope: cases where administrative penalties are not harmonised by this Regulation or where necessary, for example in cases of serious infringements
units.proposition: Member States are obliged to implement a system that provides for effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties where this Regulation does not harmonise administrative penalties or where necessary, for example in cases of serious infringements.

units.action: determine whether such penalties are criminal or administrative
units.scope: penalty systems implemented under national law pursuant to this Regulation
units.proposition: Member States have the power to determine whether penalties implemented under national law pursuant to this Regulation are criminal or administrative.

units.action: reconcile rules governing freedom of expression and information, including journalistic, academic, artistic and literary expression, with the right to the protection of personal data pursuant to this Regulation
units.scope: Member State law
units.proposition: Member States are obliged to reconcile rules governing freedom of expression and information, including journalistic, academic, artistic and literary expression, with the right to the protection of personal data pursuant to this Regulation.

units.action: subject processing of personal data solely for journalistic purposes or for academic, artistic or literary expression to derogations or exemptions from certain provisions of this Regulation as necessary to reconcile rights
units.scope: processing in the audiovisual field and in news archives and press libraries in particular
units.condition: it is necessary to reconcile the right to the protection of personal data with the right to freedom of expression and information
units.proposition: Member States are obliged to subject processing of personal data solely for journalistic purposes or for academic, artistic or literary expression to derogations or exemptions from certain provisions of this Regulation as necessary to reconcile the right to the protection of personal data with the right to freedom of expression and information.
